editorial.headline: People’s Shipping for International Cargo: What 50127 Covers
editorial.standfirst: A maritime freight activity for cargo and animals moving between Indonesian and overseas ports, open nationally to full foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA in Bali.
editorial.body:
Activity 50127 concerns people’s-shipping maritime transport carrying goods and/or animals between ports in Indonesia and ports abroad. Its working vessels are sailing ships, traditional motor vessels and motor-sailing vessels within the specified size criteria. The scope also includes the rental of that maritime transport together with its operator. In plain terms, this is an operational freight activity: the movement of cargo or animals by sea across an international port-to-port route, as well as operator-inclusive vessel hire.

The activity is open to enterprises at every listed scale: micro, small, medium and large. That breadth matters because the record does not confine the activity to a single business size or operating model. A founder considering the activity should still keep the core distinction clear: the registered business is maritime transport for goods or animals, using the vessel types set out in the scope, rather than a generic shipping label detached from a real transport operation.

Nationally, the activity is open to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. There is no lesser national foreign-share cap in the record. For Bali, the more useful question is whether provincial treatment changes that national position. Bali’s permanent, island-wide PMA moratorium blocks activities assessed as Low or Medium-Low risk. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium: at the large scale, its OSS risk is recorded as Medium-High/High. The Bali status is therefore OK or higher risk, rather than a moratorium exclusion.

That is the honest practical reading of the record. A foreign-owned business may be registered nationally with up to 100% foreign ownership, and the Bali classification does not place this activity behind the stated PMA moratorium. The Bali point is not an invented local ownership limit or special partnership condition; it is the risk-based reason the activity remains outside the provincial block. The defining question remains whether the intended operation genuinely fits the stated international maritime carriage of goods or animals and the associated operator-inclusive charter activity.
